messages:
incident-bot: Paging: KV cache eviction spike observed in prod-usw2 GPU pool. Alerts: kv.evictions/s > 1200 (baseline ~150), continuous-batcher queue depth rising, tail latency p95 > 1200ms. Incident page: https://rwd.in/incident/INC-21765 :rotating_light:

sarah: I'm on it — looking at the dashboard now. evictions correlate with a recent change to the prefetch/backpressure heuristics rolled out ~09:12 UTC. continuous-batcher config shows aggressive max_batch_age lowered, causing many tiny batches + cache churn.

mike: I see the deploy in the timeline: canary rollout at 09:10 -> 09:15. That flag is `feature.prefetch_v2` (global).

jordan: Are customer errors spiking? any 5xx from the serving runtime?

sarah: yes, a subset of tenants have elevated 5xx and increased retries; errors appear downstream as KV cache misses and eviction storms causing extra load on compute. sample tenant ids: tenant-acme-22, tenant-orion-7, tenant-beta-11.

ana: (typo: ana) I can flip a per-customer override if needed. Suggest start with a targeted rollback for the top-3 impacted tenants while we assess global rollback.

mike: Agreed. I'll try a per-tenant flag override to disable prefetch for those tenants first. Command I'm using:

```bash
# per-tenant override via redwoodctl
redwoodctl feature override set feature.prefetch_v2 false --tenant tenant-acme-22
redwoodctl feature override set feature.prefetch_v2 false --tenant tenant-orion-7
redwoodctl feature override set feature.prefetch_v2 false --tenant tenant-beta-11
```

mike: applying now.

deploy-bot: deploy status: per-tenant overrides applied (3 targets). change-id: ov-21765-1.

jordan: after overrides, evictions for those tenants down ~60% in first 30s. overall cluster evictions still elevated though.

sarah: Good. We need a fast global mitigation because continuous batching is creating many short-lived KV entries and churn. Options: 1) revert feature.prefetch_v2 globally, 2) adjust batch.window / max_batch_age to increase batching tolerance, 3) enable backpressure to throttle prefetch tasks.

mike: I'm leaning to toggle `feature.prefetch_v2` -> off globally as a hotfix canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%). It's simplest and rollback is straightforward.

ana (ana): If we do canary, do it by region to avoid cross-region cascades. start with us-west-2 5% of instances.

sarah: I'll coordinate the canary. Plan: set feature pref off for 5% of traffic in us-west-2, monitor evictions/s, latency, and error-rate for 10m. if good, 25% -> 50% -> 100%. If any regression revert.

mike: initiating canary now. Command: `redwoodctl feature rollout start feature.prefetch_v2 --region us-west-2 --percent 5 --strategy canary --description "hotfix - revert prefetch_v2 after eviction spike"`

deploy-bot: rollout started: r-21765-canary-5 (us-west-2, 5%)

jordan: metrics at +2m: canary group evictions down ~70%, p95 latency in canary nodes back to baseline. non-canary still high but trend improving.

sarah: move to 25% in 5m if still stable. Also schedule per-customer overrides for customers reporting errors until global is fully rolled out.

mike: rolling to 25% now. `redwoodctl feature rollout update r-21765-canary-5 --percent 25`

deploy-bot: rollout updated: r-21765-canary-5 -> 25%

ana: watching logs — seeing fewer small batches and KV writes dropping. There are still a few eviction hot-spikes in a single shard (shard-7). Could be hotspot tenant.

sarah: Identify top kv keys in that shard — run quick query: `SELECT top_keys FROM kv_metrics WHERE shard=7 ORDER BY writes DESC LIMIT 10`

mike: running — looks like tenant-orion-7's prefetch pattern is hammering a narrow keyspace, causing localized eviction pressure. We already disabled prefetch for orion-7 earlier which helped, but residual nodes still catching up.

jordan: Any customer-facing comms needed? Support is getting several tickets.

sarah: Send an ops note to support: short blurb that we're mitigating an infrastructure issue affecting a small subset of tenants in us-west-2; mitigation in progress, ETA 20–30m for full restore. Include IDs of impacted tenants and that per-tenant overrides applied.

leo: I'm taking the next on-call shift in 12 minutes. Sarah — want to hand off?

sarah: Yes — handing off. Current status: canary at 25% showing solid improvement, per-tenant overrides active for acme-22, orion-7, beta-11. Plan: continue staged rollout to 100% over next 15–20m if metrics remain stable, then remove overrides and keep monitoring. Follow-up: open post-incident ticket to investigate prefetch heuristics and add guardrails (max-local-prefetch, shard-level admission control).

leo: Got it. Taking over ops. Immediate actions I'll perform: 1) continue rollout to 50% -> 100% if no regression, 2) keep per-tenant overrides on until we confirm baseline for all nodes, 3) add temporary rate-limit on prefetch tasks for shard-7.

mike: rolling to 50% now. `redwoodctl feature rollout update r-21765-canary-5 --percent 50`

deploy-bot: rollout updated: r-21765-canary-5 -> 50%

ana: 10m after initial canary: whole cluster evictions down ~55% vs peak, error-rate decreased, tail latency improved ~400–600ms p95 delta back to normal range.

leo: continuing to 100%. `redwoodctl feature rollout update r-21765-canary-5 --percent 100`

deploy-bot: rollout completed: r-21765-canary-5 -> 100% (global)

jordan: Post-rollout checks: no regression signals, evictions stabilized near baseline, CPU on KV nodes decreased. Good to remove per-tenant overrides?

sarah: Let's keep overrides for another 30m, then remove for acme-22 and beta-11 first, keep orion-7 for longer because of hotspot history.

mike: removing override for tenant-acme-22: `redwoodctl feature override delete feature.prefetch_v2 --tenant tenant-acme-22`

deploy-bot: override deleted for tenant-acme-22

ana: acme-22 metrics green. remove beta-11 override.

deploy-bot: override deleted for tenant-beta-11

jordan: orion-7 still shows occasional spikes; we'll keep that override and open a follow-up (ENG-21765) to investigate hot key patterns and implement shard-level admission control + prefetch smoothing.

leo: Handing off to oncall rotation notes: incident mitigated via global feature rollback, per-tenant overrides used as temporary isolation, targeted rate limiting on shard-7. Customers notified via support. Follow-up tasks: postmortem, regression test for prefetch change, add automated circuit-breaker for prefetch in high-eviction scenarios.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident page updated: https://rwd.in/incident/INC-21765. Closing pager for now. :white_check_mark:

sarah: Thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem and link the rollout logs. handing off full notes to leo in the incident doc.

leo: got it. taking over monitoring for the next hour. ping me if anything odd shows up.

mike: small follow-up — we should also add a canary that exercises prefetch with heavy single-key access to catch hotspots in staging before large rollouts. Adding to ENG-21765.

ana: will open support summary and send to impacted customers.

incident-bot: Alert: no further anomalies in last 10m.

leo: closing thread; will update if anything changes.
